QuestionText: A computer mouse is a _________ device.
Explanation: The mouse is an input device because it sends instructions to the computer.

QuestionText: How many buttons does a standard mouse usually have?
Explanation: A standard mouse has a Left button and a Right button.

QuestionText: What is the small wheel in the middle of the mouse buttons called?
Explanation: The scroll wheel is used to move up and down on a page.

QuestionText: The arrow moving on the monitor when you move the mouse is called the _________.
Explanation: The mouse pointer (or cursor) shows the movement of the mouse on the screen.

QuestionText: To select an item on the screen, we press the left button _________.
Explanation: A single click with the left button is used to select an icon or item.

QuestionText: Pressing and releasing the left mouse button twice quickly is called _________.
Explanation: Double-clicking is used to open a program or a file.

QuestionText: Which mouse action is used to see a list of commands or options?
Explanation: Right-clicking opens a 'Shortcut Menu' with more options for an item.

QuestionText: Moving the mouse while holding the left button down is called _________.
Explanation: Dragging allows you to move items from one place to another on the screen.

QuestionText: Releasing the mouse button after dragging an item is called _________.
Explanation: The full action of moving an item is called 'Drag and Drop'.

QuestionText: Where should we always keep the mouse?
Explanation: A mouse pad provides a smooth surface for the mouse to work correctly.

QuestionText: Which finger is usually placed on the Left Mouse Button?
Explanation: The index finger of the right hand is used for the left button.

QuestionText: Which finger is usually placed on the Right Mouse Button?
Explanation: The middle finger of the right hand is used for the right button.

QuestionText: What does a mouse look like?
Options: A) A real mouse with a tail
B) A box with a screen
Explanation: It is a small, hand-held device shaped roughly like an oval.

QuestionText: The wire of the mouse is connected to the _________.
Explanation: The mouse wire (the 'tail') connects to the CPU to send signals.

QuestionText: A wireless mouse works without a _________.
Explanation: Wireless mice use signals instead of a physical wire to talk to the computer.

QuestionText: Which part of the mouse helps us go through a long story on the screen?
Explanation: Scrolling up and down helps read long documents or websites.

QuestionText: When you move the mouse to the right, the pointer on the screen moves _________.
Explanation: The pointer follows the exact direction of the mouse movement.

QuestionText: To open a game on the desktop, you should _________ its icon.
Explanation: Double-clicking is the standard way to launch an application.

QuestionText: Should we click the mouse buttons very hard?
Explanation: Clicking too hard can break the sensitive switches inside the mouse.

QuestionText: Optical mice use _________ instead of a ball to track movement.
Explanation: Optical mice use a red or blue light sensor to see how they are moving.

QuestionText: What happens when you scroll the wheel forward (up)?
Explanation: Scrolling up moves the view toward the top of the page.

QuestionText: Which hand is the mouse designed for most commonly?
Explanation: While left-handed mice exist, most standard mice are shaped for the right hand.

QuestionText: You should rest your _________ on the back of the mouse.
Explanation: Resting your palm on the mouse helps you control it better without getting tired.

QuestionText: A mouse is used to _________ on the computer screen.
Explanation: Mice are great for drawing, painting, and selecting items.

QuestionText: If the mouse pointer is not moving, what should you check?
Explanation: If the wire is loose, the mouse cannot send signals to the CPU.

QuestionText: Which button is clicked to open the Start menu with the mouse?
Explanation: You left-click on the Start icon to open the menu.

QuestionText: Double-click means clicking the button _________ times.
Explanation: Double means two.

QuestionText: Can you use a mouse without a mouse pad?
Options: A) Yes, but it's better with one
Explanation: It works on most flat surfaces, but a mouse pad protects the mouse from dust.

QuestionText: What does the pointer usually look like?
Explanation: The default pointer is a small slanted arrow.

QuestionText: Which action would you use to move a file into a folder?
Explanation: Drag and drop is the standard way to move files between folders.

QuestionText: The mouse pointer changes to a _________ when you can type text.
Explanation: The pointer changes shape based on what you are doing; an 'I' shape means you can type there.

QuestionText: If the mouse has a ball underneath, it is a _________ mouse.
Explanation: Old-style mice with a rolling ball are called mechanical mice.

QuestionText: To keep the mouse clean, we should _________.
Options: A) Wipe it with a dry cloth
B) Dip it in soapy water
Explanation: Gently wiping with a dry or slightly damp cloth keeps it dust-free.

QuestionText: Clicking the right mouse button once is called _________.
Explanation: Using the right button is called a right-click.

QuestionText: Which mouse part is used to zoom in or out in some programs?
Explanation: In many apps, holding a key while scrolling zooms the screen.

QuestionText: The mouse is usually kept to the _________ side of the keyboard.
Explanation: For most users, the mouse sits on the right side of the keyboard.

QuestionText: Does a laptop have a mouse?
Options: D) Only if you plug one in
Explanation: Laptops have a built-in touchpad that works just like a mouse.

QuestionText: When the pointer turns into a small hand, it usually means you can _________.
Explanation: A hand icon usually appears over buttons or links on the internet.

QuestionText: How should you hold the mouse?
Explanation: Hold it lightly so you can move it easily and click precisely.

QuestionText: What happens if you move the mouse on a very bumpy surface?
Explanation: Mice need a flat surface to track movement smoothly.

QuestionText: If you are left-handed, can you change mouse settings?
Options: B) Yes, to swap the buttons
D) Only with a new mouse
Explanation: Computers allow you to swap the left and right button functions for left-handed people.

QuestionText: The scroll wheel is located _________.
Explanation: It is positioned right in the center for easy access.

QuestionText: Which click do you use to select a word in a document?
Explanation: In most text editors, a double-click selects the whole word.

QuestionText: Dragging an item means to _________.
Options: B) Move it while holding the button
Explanation: Dragging is the movement part of moving an icon.

QuestionText: What does 'Click' sound like?
Explanation: Mouse buttons make a light clicking sound when pressed.

QuestionText: If the mouse pointer turns into a spinning circle, it means the computer is _________.
Explanation: A spinning circle or hourglass means you should wait for the computer to finish its task.

QuestionText: Can a mouse be used to play games?
Explanation: Many computer games use the mouse for movement and action.

QuestionText: A mouse pad helps to keep the mouse _________.
Explanation: Mouse pads prevent dust from getting into the sensors or rollers.

QuestionText: Which action helps you see more content at the bottom of a webpage?
Explanation: Scrolling down reveals the hidden part of the page below the screen.

QuestionText: The mouse helps us to give _________ to the computer.
Explanation: Clicking is a way of telling the computer what to do.
